provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program scans the visible grid directly. A row is filled when every cell in its interior span grid[y, 1:W-1] is the open colour palette[0]. Each such row has that span painted palette[3]. Columns get the same test over grid[1:H-1, x]. Both tests read the original input, so painting rows cannot block columns, and cells where a filled row meets a filled column stay palette[3]. This also matches the generator's 'nonzero cell = blocked' check, since 0 becomes palette[0] under the palette. Rotating or reflecting the grid swaps rows with columns and maps interior to interior, so the same two scans are correct in every visible orientation. Only the two colour constants are specialised, and d4 needs no change in direction. The wall colours (2 and 8) are not hard-coded: any cell that is not palette[0] counts as a blocker. Rectangular grids work because H and W are used separately.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes a one-cell outer frame, with open space marked by exactly palette[0], as in the constructor. Grids smaller than 3 in either dimension are returned unchanged. Demonstrations are not used, because the colour roles follow fully from the palette. No contradictions with the fixtures were found: all three train pairs and the test pair match this rule. I have not run any tests.
